vocabulary.meaning_en: wanting to know more about something
making people want to know more
tired = how you feel; tiring = what makes you tired
vocabulary.example: The trip was tiring, so I was tired.

vocabulary.meaning_en: surprised = how you feel; surprising = causing surprise
vocabulary.example: She had a surprised smile. The news was surprising.

vocabulary.meaning_en: receiving an action, not doing it
vocabulary.example: "Bored" is passive: you receive the feeling.
"Boring" is active: it causes the feeling.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a verb that joins the subject to a description: be, seem, look, feel
vocabulary.example: In "He seems interested", "seems" is a linking verb.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the state or situation of something
vocabulary.example: "Crowded" describes the condition of the room.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a short review of the main points
vocabulary.example: Here is a quick recap of the lesson.

fine_lines.title: bored vs boring
fine_lines.explanation_ar: -ed: الشخص يتلقى الشعور (I am bored = أشعر بالملل). -ing: الشيء أو الشخص يسبّب الشعور للآخرين (The film is boring = الفيلم ممل). انتبه: He is boring = هو ممل للآخرين، He is bored = هو يشعر بالملل.
fine_lines.explanation_en: -ed: the person receives the feeling (I am bored). -ing: the thing or person causes the feeling (The film is boring). Careful: "He is boring" = he makes others bored; "He is bored" = he feels bored.

examples.sentence: I was bored, so I left early.

fine_lines.title: interested vs interesting
fine_lines.explanation_ar: interested = أنا مهتم (شعوري). interesting = الشيء مثير للاهتمام (يسبب الشعور).
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Interested" = how I feel. "Interesting" = the thing that causes the feeling.

expressions.meaning_en: He looks like he wants to know more.
expressions.example: Tell him about the course. He seems interested.

Let me clear that up for you.

grammar.title: -ed adjectives: passive, received, finished
grammar.explanation_ar: الصفة المنتهية بـ ed تأتي من فعل، وتعني أنك تلقيت أثر الفعل (مبني للمجهول) وأن الفعل انتهى، فتصف شعورك: bored, tired, excited. وتصف أيضًا حالة الشيء الآن بعد فعل انتهى: a crowded room, a heated argument.
grammar.explanation_en: -ed adjectives come from verbs. They mean you received the action (passive) and the action is finished, so they describe your feeling: bored, tired, excited. They also describe a condition now, after a finished action: a crowded room, a heated argument.
examples: I felt tired after the long trip.

grammar.title: -ing adjectives: active, causing, ongoing
grammar.explanation_ar: الصفة المنتهية بـ ing فعّالة: تسبب الشعور للآخرين الآن (boring, tiring, interesting)، أو تصف فعلًا مستمرًا (a growing business = عمل يكبر باستمرار).
grammar.explanation_en: -ing adjectives are active: they cause a feeling in others now (boring, tiring, interesting), or describe an ongoing action (a growing business = a business that keeps getting bigger).

grammar.title: Word order: before nouns, after linking verbs
grammar.explanation_ar: تأتي هذه الصفات قبل الاسم (an interesting man, a surprised smile) أو بعد فعل رابط مثل be / seem / look (He seems interested).
grammar.explanation_en: These adjectives go before a noun (an interesting man, a surprised smile) or after a linking verb like be / seem / look (He seems interested).

grammar.title: Degree: so, very, the most
grammar.explanation_ar: نستعمل الظروف so و very لنبين الدرجة، و the most للتفضيل: so interesting, very bored, the most interesting actor.
grammar.explanation_en: Use the adverbs "so" and "very" for degree, and "the most" for the superlative: so interesting, very bored, the most interesting actor.
examples: He is the most interesting teacher in the school.
